summary: Delayed session affinity to pinned model during sudden backpressure burst causing fallback to degraded variant
description:
Issue summary:
During a customer-triggered heavy traffic spike (short burst of high QPS) in their dedicated pool we observed a delay in the control-plane committing session affinity to the customer's pinned model version. As a result a subset of session streams were routed to the fallback (degraded/int8) variant, producing inconsistent outputs for NarrativeAI's users.

Impact:
- Approximately 12% of requests for this tenant over a 7m window returned responses from the degraded variant instead of the pinned full-precision model.
- Customers reported quality regressions and increased API latency.
- No 5xx errors were observed; this is routing/coherence degradation only.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-03-10 14:02: customer traffic spike begins (~3x baseline for 6 minutes).
- 2026-03-10 14:03: edge health probes see increased latency; orchestrator starts backpressure mitigation.
- 2026-03-10 14:04: control-plane commit of session-affinity to pinned variant delayed by ~90s due to coordinator queueing.
- 2026-03-10 14:09: routing stabilizes and pinned affinity applied; traffic returns to expected variant.

Steps to reproduce (local / test):
1) Simulate sustained short-duration QPS spike against a tenant with model_version pin and canary weight 5%.
2) Inject artificial probe latency on selected edge nodes to trigger orchestrator backpressure path.
3) Observe control-plane commit latency and routing decisions in the cohort.

Observed logs / snippets:
- edge-proxy: "WARN 14:03:23 queue_delay=120ms backpressure=throttled tenant=narra-123"
- orchestrator: "INFO 14:04:02 commit-request queued reason=probe-latency queue_len=18"
- control-plane: "DEBUG 14:04:45 session-affinity-commit tenant=narra-123 version=gptx-13b-v2 latency=92s"
- serving-runtime: "INFO 14:05:01 routed-request variant=gptx-13b-int8 reason=fallback-capacity"

Workaround implemented:
- Support placed a short-lived override to prioritize pending commit for tenant narra-123 (manual bump on orchestrator) at 14:05 which accelerated affinity commit.
- Suggested customer increase canary weight to 20% for staging ripples or temporarily disable automatic backpressure for this tenant's pool (customer elected to keep).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: coordinator queueing and commit-worker starvation during burst delayed the affinity commit path.
Confirmed control-plane commit latency spikes correlate with orchestrator queue length and edge probe latencies.
Serving runtime correctly reported fallback routing decisions when pinned variant not yet committed at the edge.
No evidence of KV cache corruption; keys show consistent session tokens but routing table lacked committed mapping until commit applied.
Related: behavior resembles SUP-4721 but root cause appears to be backpressure queueing rather than cache TTL mismatch.
SRE reproduced in staging by combining health-probe slowdown and commit-worker CPU starvation (CPU limiter set low on commit-worker pod).
comments: 2026-03-10 14:15 - Lina Chen (SRE): I pushed a manual priority ticket to the orchestrator for narra-123 which forced immediate commit; observing routing shifting back to pinned variant.

2026-03-10 15:03 - Marco Ruiz (Support): Reached out to NarrativeAI (CS rep Emma Holt) to confirm impact window and whether customers have ongoing errors; customer reports quality complaints but no data loss.

2026-03-10 16:22 - Emma Holt (NarrativeAI): We saw mismatched responses in our chat logs during 14:02-14:09 UTC. We're attaching sample conversation IDs for QA. We are on dedicated tier and would like mitigation steps to avoid recurrence.

2026-03-11 09:10 - SRE Oncall: Reproduced in staging. We observed commit-worker CPU throttling coincident with orchestrator queue growth. Increasing commit-worker CPU to 500m in staging removed the delay in our test.
2026-03-12 11:45 - Marco Ruiz (Support): Coordinated a customer-facing summary and scheduled a follow-up meeting with NarrativeAI for 2026-03-15 to discuss quota/backpressure tuning and SLA remedies.
resolution_notes:
Mitigation applied in-prod: increased commit-worker CPU request on affected orchestrator nodes from 200m -> 500m, and added a short-term priority path so pending pin-commits for dedicated tenants escalate under backpressure. Config changes rolled 2026-03-11 02:30 UTC. Observed commit latency for similar test spikes dropped from ~90s to <3s in staging.
Follow-ups: engineering task created to add adaptive backpressure aware commit-scheduling (ENG-issue: https://github.com/redwood/serving/issues/6134). Recommend adding a canary gating check to avoid applying backpressure to control-plane commit queues for tenants with active pins.
Customer communication: assigned CS owner to send summary and proposed remediation; customer accepted the workaround and requested notification on the production rollout of the adaptive scheduler.
next_steps: ENG to scope adaptive commit scheduler that treats pin-commit operations as high-priority under tenant-dedicated pools (owner: Marco Ruiz / due 2026-04-02).
Add runbook step: detect commit-worker queue_len > 10 and auto-scale commit-workers or temporarily bypass backpressure for pin-commits (owner: Lina Chen).
Monitor: create Grafana alert for 'commit_latency > 5s' per-tenant and link to oncall channel #support (owner: Observability).
Customer follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-03-15 to review root cause and confirm acceptance of remediation.
